if: an estimate is revised because circumstances changed, or because of new information, more experience or subsequent developments
then: the revision is NOT an extraordinary item and NOT a prior period item
note: AS 5 para 18 gives the discriminating example: income or expense recognised on the outcome of a contingency that previously could not be estimated reliably does not constitute a prior period item. The prior statements were not wrong; the information did not exist yet.

evidence.quote: An estimate may have to be revised if changes occur regarding the circumstances on which the estimate was based, or as a result of new information, more experience or subsequent developments.
the definitions of an extraordinary item or a prior period item.

evidence.quote: Prior period items are generally infrequent in nature and can be distinguished from changes in accounting estimates. Accounting estimates by their nature are approximations that may need revision as additional information becomes known. For example, income or expense recognised on the outcome of a contingency which previously could not be estimated reliably does not constitute a prior period item.
